newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Primakov says NATO-Russia talks to be decisive.
newsitem.headline: Primakov says NATO-Russia talks to be decisive.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Sunday talks between Moscow and NATO this week would show whether the former Cold War foes can sign a security deal on May 27.

He told Russia Television progress had been made at negotiations on forging a peaceful new relationship, but he could not guarantee that his talks with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana in Moscow on Tuesday would solve all problems.
"There are still some loose ends, some issues which have to be resolved, and the negotiations will continue right until the end," Primakov said in an interview recorded on May 8.
"But already on May 13 or 14, when General Secretary Solana is in Moscow, it will be clear whether we can get to sign the document on May 27 or not."
Asked if it was still possible an agreement would not be signed on the May 27 target date set by President Boris Yeltsin, Primakov replied: "I can't rule that out."

Yeltsin said last Thursday a document on Russia's relations with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation was "98 percent" ready and he might join the coming talks in Moscow to try to finalise the deal.
Russia opposes NATO's plans to expand eastwards to take in new members from the former Soviet bloc.

But he has signalled he wants a deal on terms for a new partnership with NATO, and as many concessions as possible, before the Western defence alliance issue the first new membership invitations in July.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are thought to be top of the list to join, but Romania and Slovenia also hope to be in the first wave of new members.
